key_insight: LLM agents can serve as practical natural-language schedulers for home energy management, translating household preferences into near-optimal appliance plans under dynamic prices and solar forecasts.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that tool-calling LLMs can bridge user-friendly control and MILP-grade scheduling performance for residential demand response and device optimization.
method: Built a ReAct-style tool-calling agent using live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, household usage data, and retrieval-augmented knowledge.
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP ground truth across tariff, conflict, and weather-aware scenarios.
Compared native function calling with text-parsed actions and tested week-long simulated deployment performance.
evidence_signal: Across benchmark scenarios, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success and near-MILP optimality, and week-long agents captured 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings, projecting about GBP 1,270 annual savings over an off-peak timer baseline.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply when relying on text-parsed actions, so robust function-calling and constraint handling are critical for real deployments.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
